newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania, Italy agree to halt illegal immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Albania, Italy agree to halt illegal immigrants.

text.p: Albania and Italy on Monday pledged to step up cooperation between their police forces to fight organised crime and the flow of illegal immigrants.

Italian Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano, on an official visit to Tirana, signed an agreement with his Albanian counterpart Halit Shamata to try to halt the smuggling of illegal immigrants into Italy.
Smuggling and a rise in organised crime has soared since Albania toppled its communist regime six years ago.
"The fight against the illegal traffic of immigrants and organised crime will become possible through more concrete and continuous cooperation between our two police forces," Shamata told reporters.
Napolitano said Italy was ready to cooperate more on legal immigration of Albanians, but added that both countries would intensify work to stop the influx of illegal immigrants.
"Italy does not have a closed-door policy. Albanians may come legally...but not in an unlimited number and not in an uncontrolled manner," Napolitano said.

Hundreds of immigrants enter Italy illegally each year from Albania by crossing a narrow strait in the Adriatic sea between the two countries. The Italian government last year sent troops to beaches in Puglia to try to stem the influx of illegal Albanian immigrants.
